_comment: The 74 expert-defined MRI diagnoses from NeuroVFM Supplementary Data Figure 6 (MRI diagnosis extraction prompt). Order and key names are verbatim from the caption. 'guidance' holds the parenthetical clarification given in the caption (empty string if none). Injected into the extraction prompt where the caption reads '<diagnoses, refer to caption>'.

diagnoses.guidance: "yes" if radiologist confident for cavernoma; "no" if possible microbleed
"yes" for acute ischemia/infarct with diffusion restriction
"yes" for chronic or evolving ischemia/infarct without diffusion restriction
also known as microvascular ischemic disease
"yes" for any intracranial hemorrhage, excluding microhemorrhage
"yes" for hemorrhages within the brain, usually spontaneous and due to hypertension
"yes" if due to ruptured aneurysm or other vascular cause
"yes" if due to head trauma
"yes" if radiologist is confident for brain abscesses or subdural empyemas
most commonly herpes encephalitis involving the temporal and frontal lobes
"yes" for intracranial epidermoid cyst only
"yes" for any intracranial mass, growth, or neoplasm
"yes" for any orbital mass, growth, or neoplasm
"yes" for tumor/cancer in the oral cavity, throat, larynx, nasal cavity, salivary, and thyroid gland
"yes" for any spine mass, growth, or neoplasm
"yes" for nerve, nerve root, or nerve sheath tumors
"yes" if mostly likely primary glial tumor
"yes" if MRI features for high-grade glioma
"yes" if MRI features for low-grade glioma
"yes" for any tumor in the pineal region
diagnosis includes, but not limited to, medulloblastoma, ependymoma, pilocytic astrocytoma
diagnosis also called diffuse midline gliomas
"yes" for chiari I/II malformations
"yes" for any abnormally enlarged ventricles
"yes" for ventriculomegaly due to brain atrophy, normal pressure hydrocephalus, or ex vacuo dilation
"yes" for ventriculomegaly due to mass lesion or aqueductal stenosis
"yes" for any intracranial catheter
